target: Dyna'r tŷ adeiladodd fy nhad-cu.
english: That's the house my grandfather built.
tip: Welsh often drops 'that' in relative clauses: Dyna'r tŷ adeiladodd fy nhad-cu = the house my grandfather built.

target: Dw i wedi torri fy mraich.
english: I've broken my arm.
tip: fy (my) turns b into m: braich becomes fy mraich (my arm).

target: Mae'r afon yn ddyfnach fan hyn.
english: The river is deeper here.
tip: Add -ach to an adjective for the comparative: dwfn (deep) gives the ddyfnach here (deeper).

target: Rydw i am rannu fy marn.
english: I want to share my opinion.
tip: am before a verb-noun means 'want to' or 'intend to': am rannu here is 'want to share'.

target: Mae fy nhad-cu yn naw deg pump.
english: My grandfather is ninety-five.
tip: Modern Welsh counts in tens: naw deg pump is nine-ten-five, that is ninety-five.

target: Mae mis Mehefin yn dechrau'r haf swyddogol.
english: June marks the start of official summer.
tip: Month names take mis in front: mis Mehefin is literally 'month of June'.

target: Fy nhad a ddysgodd fi i bysgota.
english: It was my father who taught me to fish.
tip: Front the subject and add a for emphasis: Fy nhad a ddysgodd = it was my father who taught.

target: Oddi wrth fy mam ces i'r llythyr.
english: It was from my mother I got the letter.
tip: ces i is the past of cael (to get): ces i'r llythyr = I got the letter.

target: Mae mis Mawrth yn dod â gwyntoedd cryfion.
english: March brings strong winds.
tip: Adjectives can take a plural form beside plural nouns: cryf (strong) becomes cryfion for gwyntoedd.

target: Roedd e bob amser yn darllen cyn mynd i'r gwely.
english: He would always read before bed.
tip: Roedd plus a verb-noun means 'used to': Roedd e bob amser yn darllen = he used to read.

target: Byddwn i wrth fy modd yn ymweld â Phatagonia ryw ddiwrnod.
english: I'd love to visit Patagonia one day.
tip: Byddwn i means 'I would', the conditional of bod: Byddwn i wrth fy modd = I'd love it.

target: Mae fy nghefn yn brifo ar ôl gweithio yn yr ardd.
english: My back hurts after working in the garden.
tip: ar ôl (after) is followed by a verb-noun: ar ôl gweithio = after working.

target: Dyna oedd y storm waethaf ers blynyddoedd.
english: That was the worst storm in years.
tip: gwaethaf means 'worst', an irregular superlative of drwg (bad); it appears here as waethaf.

target: Dyna'r afon lle mae'r eogiaid yn silio.
english: That's the river where the salmon spawn.
tip: lle means 'where', linking a place to what happens in it: yr afon lle mae'r eogiaid yn silio.

target: Mae'r deallusrwydd artiffisial yn dysgu o batrymau data.
english: Artificial intelligence learns from data patterns.
tip: o (from) softens the next word: patrymau becomes o batrymau, p changing to b.

target: Gyda phobl hŷn, defnyddiwch 'chi' ar y dechrau.
english: With older people, use 'chi' at first.
tip: chi is the polite or plural 'you'; ti is for friends and children.

target: Dw i'n debyg i fy nhad mewn llawer o ffyrdd.
english: I'm similar to my father in many ways.
tip: debyg (similar) is followed by i for 'to': debyg i fy nhad = similar to my father.

target: Dw i wedi brifo fy ffêr wrth gerdded ar y mynydd.
english: I've hurt my ankle while walking on the mountain.
tip: wedi plus a verb-noun makes the perfect: Dw i wedi brifo = I have hurt.

target: Bob tro mae'n bwrw eira, mae'r plant yn adeiladu dyn eira.
english: Every time it snows, the children build a snowman.
tip: yn before a verb-noun makes an ongoing action: mae'r plant yn adeiladu = the children are building.

target: Rwy'n hynod falch o fod yn Gymro ac o siarad iaith fy nhad-cu a'm mam-gu.
english: I'm incredibly proud to be Welsh and to speak the language of my grandparents.
tip: Rwy'n is a common 'I am', short for Rydw i yn: Rwy'n falch = I'm proud.

target: Mae Dylan Thomas yn fardd enwog.
english: Dylan Thomas is a famous poet.
tip: After yn a noun softens its first letter: bardd (poet) becomes yn fardd here.

target: Bangor yw'r ddinas hynaf yng Nghymru.
english: Bangor is the oldest city in Wales.
tip: yw links two nouns as equal: Bangor yw'r ddinas hynaf = Bangor is the oldest city.

target: Mae'r ŵyl yn dathlu diwylliant a cherddoriaeth Cymru.
english: The festival celebrates Welsh culture and music.
tip: a (and) triggers an aspirate change: cerddoriaeth becomes a cherddoriaeth, c turning to ch.

target: Yfwch ddigon o ddŵr.
english: Drink plenty of water.
tip: The ending -wch gives a polite or plural command: yfed (to drink) becomes Yfwch (drink).

target: Maen nhw'n byw yng Nghaernarfon.
english: They live in Caernarfon.
tip: yn (in) plus Caernarfon gives yng Nghaernarfon: c changes to ngh and yn becomes yng before it.

target: Mae ei phlant hi'n ifanc.
english: Her children are young.
tip: ei meaning her adds an h in spelling: plant becomes ei phlant; ei meaning his would give ei blant instead.

target: Mae hynny'n mynd dan fy nghroen.
english: That gets under my skin.
tip: mynd dan fy nghroen literally means going under my skin, the set phrase for something that irritates you.

target: Mae'r grawnfwyd yn boblogaidd gyda phlant.
english: Cereal is popular with children.
tip: gyda (with) adds a breath after p: plant becomes gyda phlant, p changing to ph.

target: Mae fy ngwraig i'n dod o Bontypridd.
english: My wife comes from Pontypridd.
tip: o (from) softens the next word: Pontypridd becomes o Bontypridd, p turning into b.

target: Mae'r nyrs yn dweud bod fy mhwysedd gwaed yn iawn.
english: The nurse says my blood pressure is fine.
tip: fy (my) nasal-mutates the next word: pwysedd becomes fy mhwysedd, p changing to mh.
